text:
jen (support): heads up — customer reported an SSE stream that finishes but the final JSON object never arrives. no finish_reason and client sees truncated JSON. asking for eng help. :thinking:

sara (customer): reproducing now, ~30% of attempts cut right before the closing brace. nothing in app logs other than connection closed.

jen (support): @marco @li can you take a quick look? trace id: trace_8b7f3b. they said this started after we rolled a short TTL refresh on their auth token last week.

opsbot: New ticket created: INF-4892 (linked to trace_8b7f3b)

marco (eng-runtime): can you paste the exact curl and sample output (raw bytes)? curious if client sees RST or clean close. any proxy or auth-handoff in path? :eyes:

sara (customer): here — using corporate proxy that refreshes tokens. curl command:

```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <short_lived_token>" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=open-llm-x" \
  --no-buffer
```

Sample tail from client (truncated):
```
{"id":"resp_abc","object":"chunk","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"...final words"}}],
```
then connection closes. no final `}` or `finish_reason` or trailing sentinel.

li (eng-ml): i can repro locally hitting our staging edge + inserting a token rotate in midstream. i see the edge issues a 204 during token refresh and then connection teardown. looks like the last flush isn't flushed across the auth-handoff boundary.

marco (eng-runtime): hypothesis: our TTL refresh path (auth proxy) performs a non-atomic handoff — the client connection is proxied while we request new creds, and certain keepalive/idle timers cause the upstream socket to close before the final event is emitted. that would produce an incomplete trailing object.

jen (support): customer confirms they only added the short TTL auth refresh last week. they can reproduce by triggering a rotate while a stream is open.

marco (eng-runtime): can you capture a pcap or server side stream frames? also need the proxy config (timeouts, keepalive).

sara (customer): attaching minimal repro steps:
1) open curl stream as above
2) POST to their idp to force token refresh for same session
3) watch curl output close without final object

marco (eng-runtime): thanks. reproducer locally: run `make repro-ttl-rotate` which triggers an auth handoff after 4s. i see last event bytes stuck in local buffer then connection closed. adding a `flush()` across the handoff makes the final object appear.

li (eng-ml): workaround for customers until we patch: increase proxy idle keepalive to >30s and have client reconnect/resume with an idempotent resume header. we'll also recommend the client wait for an explicit trailing sentinel (we can add one server-side).

jen (support): can you suggest a concrete customer-facing message? they asked if this is a billing/latency issue.

marco (eng-runtime): message: "This is caused by midstream token rotation at the proxy boundary which can cause the TCP connection to close before the final SSE event is flushed. We're rolling a fix to ensure we flush the final event across auth handoffs. In the meantime please extend your proxy keepalive and use the resume header to avoid losing the final chunk."

opsbot: deploy started: staging/debug-flush (job #deploy-789)

marco (eng-runtime): action items: 1) add explicit final sentinel event on stream finalization (PR in review), 2) instrument last-event flush metrics, 3) add logs to capture close reason for 4xx/204 handoffs.

jen (support): i'll reply to customer with the workaround + ETA for fix. collecting pcap and proxy timeout settings now.

sara (customer): thanks — will send pcap and proxy config. appreciate the quick triage. :pray:

marco (eng-runtime): thanks, will prioritize. ETA for staged fix ~24–48h, then we can push to prod behind a small toggle.

jen (support): marking follow-ups in INF-4892 and will update when staging verifies the sentinel flush resolves the truncated-tail case.

opsbot: INF-4892 updated: label=triaged, priority=high

jen (support): closing loop here for now, will post when staging confirms the sentinel flush resolves the truncated-tail case.
